summary: Created a managed systemd service `inventory-worker` on node1 running as a dedicated unprivileged user, sandboxed with NoNewPrivileges=yes and ProtectSystem=strict plus ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory (all other sandboxing hardening options also applied). Verified confinement: writes to /etc fail with Read-only file system while writes inside /var/lib/inventory succeed. Ran the mandatory restart protocol on node1: captured pre-restart boot id and healthy service/data state, issued `systemctl reboot`, polled until reachable, confirmed the boot id changed, and verified the service auto-started (enabled+active) and resumed writing to the same persisted data files with the sandbox properties intact.
actions_performed: Created system user inventory-worker (no home, nologin shell)
Wrote worker script /usr/local/bin/inventory-worker.sh that loops writing a log and counter into /var/lib/inventory
Wrote hardened systemd unit /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service (NoNewPrivileges, ProtectSystem=strict, ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory, plus additional sandboxing directives)
Enabled and started inventory-worker.service, verified active status and data being written
Ran a negative test transient unit confirming writes outside /var/lib/inventory fail (Read-only file system) while writes inside succeed
Captured pre-restart boot id and service/data health on node1
Issued systemctl reboot on node1, acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until reachable, confirmed boot id changed

Verified post-restart: service enabled+active, worker script resumed, prior data files present with new entries appended, sandbox properties (NoNewPrivileges, ProtectSystem, ReadWritePaths, User) unchanged

evidence.requirement: inventory-worker running as managed systemd service, confined to /var/lib/inventory, NoNewPrivileges
evidence.summary: Service created, enabled, started; systemctl show confirms NoNewPrivileges=yes, ProtectSystem=strict, ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory, User=inventory-worker; data files present under /var/lib/inventory

evidence.requirement: Confinement actually enforced (writes outside path blocked, inside allowed)
evidence.summary: Transient unit with same sandbox settings: write to /etc/inventory-escape-test fails with 'Read-only file system'; write to /var/lib/inventory/escape-check succeeds
Captured boot id 377b5195-... and confirmed service active/enabled with counter=5 and log entries present
systemctl reboot dispatched in background; 'reboot command dispatched' not printed because exec stream closed as node went down, confirming reboot took effect

evidence.requirement: Node unreachable during restart, then boot identity changed
evidence.summary: Connection timed out while node was down; subsequent poll succeeded with new boot id 5ad6e78d-... (differs from pre-restart 377b5195-...) and uptime -s showing new boot time

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of service, sandboxing, and data
evidence.summary: Service is enabled+active after reboot, resumed writing to the same inventory.log/counter files, and systemctl show confirms sandbox properties unchanged
